record.title: GUI-SD-v2 reports higher mobile GUI-agent success after privilege-following and step-level memory distillation
record.summary: An arXiv preprint introduces GUI-SD-v2, which trains a mobile GUI agent in two stages: first to follow corrective privileged guidance, then to distill step-specific reasoning and task-relevant memory from its own interaction trajectories. With Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B and Kimi-K3-generated supervision, the authors report 67.2%/79.3% Pass@1/Pass@3 on AndroidWorld and 25.6%/31.6% on the GUI-only MobileWorld subset, above the paper’s evaluated baselines under its settings. These are author-reported results on two mobile benchmark settings; code and data were stated as future releases, and neither independent reproduction nor broader transfer was established.
organizations: Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv preprint presents GUI-SD-v2, a two-stage on-policy self-distillation method for multi-turn GUI agents. Stage one jointly trains rollouts with and without corrective privileged guidance; stage two distills step-specific reasoning and memory signals into action and memory outputs.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Using Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B, the paper reports 67.2% Pass@1 and 79.3% Pass@3 on AndroidWorld, and 25.6% and 31.6% on the GUI-only MobileWorld subset. These are author-reported benchmark results; no independent reproduction was performed.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Under fixed training tasks and Kimi-K3-generated supervision, the paper reports GUI-SD-v2 above its evaluated SFT, GRPO, naive OPSD and GUI-SD-v1 baselines on both benchmarks and Pass@1/Pass@3 metrics. This is a within-paper comparison, not evidence of general superiority across models, environments or task distributions.

evidence_gaps.description: All reported benchmark results and ablations are from the paper; code and training data are described as future releases and were not available in the inspected paper.

Evaluation is limited to Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B on AndroidWorld and the GUI-only MobileWorld subset; transfer to other model sizes, desktop/web interfaces, broader task distributions or production reliability is not established.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported gains hold, transferring privileged reasoning and task-relevant memory into an 8B mobile GUI policy could improve multi-step interaction training on constrained devices and change post-training choices. The evidence is one paper’s results on two mobile benchmark settings, not broad desktop-agent reliability or independent validation.
limitations: This is a single unreviewed arXiv preprint; results are author-reported and were not independently reproduced.
Experiments use one base model, Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B, and mobile Android environments.
MobileWorld results cover its GUI-only subset, not the entire benchmark.
Training uses Kimi-K3-generated guidance and selected OpenMobile/MobileForge tasks; transfer beyond this supervision and task mix is unknown.
The paper states code and training data will be released; this activation did not verify a release.
Benchmark pass rates do not establish broad long-horizon reliability or production behavior.
organizations: Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences
brief.summary: An arXiv preprint introduces GUI-SD-v2, which trains a mobile GUI agent in two stages: first to follow corrective privileged guidance, then to distill step-specific reasoning and task-relevant memory from its own interaction trajectories. With Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B and Kimi-K3-generated supervision, the authors report 67.2%/79.3% Pass@1/Pass@3 on AndroidWorld and 25.6%/31.6% on the GUI-only MobileWorld subset, above the paper’s evaluated baselines under its settings. These are author-reported results on two mobile benchmark settings; code and data were stated as future releases, and neither independent reproduction nor broader transfer was established.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report GUI-SD-v2 improves Pass@1/Pass@3 over evaluated baselines on AndroidWorld and the GUI-only MobileWorld subset using Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper specifies the two-stage method, benchmark settings and reported results; this activation re-read the paper but did not execute experiments.
technical.implementation_status: Research preprint. The paper says code and training data will be released; no release was verified in this review.
technical.mechanism: Privilege-following optimization jointly trains original-context and corrective-guidance rollouts. Informative privilege distillation then transfers step-specific reasoning and memory guidance from a self-teacher conditioned on privileged context into the same policy’s action and memory outputs.
technical.regime: Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B in Android emulator environments; selected OpenMobile/MobileForge training tasks with Kimi-K3-generated supervision; evaluation on AndroidWorld and the GUI-only MobileWorld subset.
technical.strongest_baseline: Within the paper: same training-task scale and Kimi-K3 supervision for SFT, GRPO, naive OPSD and GUI-SD-v1; also reported comparisons with selected GUI-agent systems. No independent matched reproduction.

brief.title: GUI-SD-v2 reports higher mobile GUI-agent success after privilege-following and step-level memory distillation
brief.why_it_matters: The method targets a concrete bottleneck in multi-turn interface agents: a policy may receive useful privileged hints but fail to follow them or retain task state. If the reported gains reproduce, training the same policy to use step-level reasoning and memory guidance could improve mobile-agent post-training. The evidence remains benchmark-bounded and does not establish general agent reliability.
